Rashi on Sotah 26a:12:1.hebrew: והיא לא נתפשה כו' - כלומר, מהו דתימא פרשת סוטה על כרחך באשת ישראל קיימא, מדכתיב "והיא" — מיעוטא משמע, זו היא דכי לא נתפשה אסורה, הא נתפשה כו'. ועלה קאי קרא דבתריה "ועבר עליו רוח" וגו', דהיכא דמספקא לן בהך אם נטמאה ואם לא נטמאה — שותה. אבל אשת כהן דליתה בכלל "והיא לא נתפשה", ליתה נמי בכלל השקאה. קמ"ל:
Rashi on Sotah 26a:12:1.english: "And she was not caught," etc. - That is, what might you have said? The passage of the sota must, perforce, be speaking of the wife of an Israelite, since it is written "and she" — which implies a limitation: it is this woman who, when she was not caught, is forbidden [to her husband]; [implying that] if she was caught [i.e., she was forced], etc. And the verse that follows, "And a spirit of jealousy comes over him" etc., is stated in reference to this: that where we are uncertain about her — whether she became defiled or did not become defiled — she drinks. But the wife of a priest, who is not included in "and she was not caught," is also not included in the giving of the water to drink. [Therefore] it teaches us [that she does drink].

Rashi on Sotah 26a:13:1.hebrew: במתנוונה - לאחר ששתתה איצטריך לאשמועינן דמותרת לבעלה, דלא תימא זונה היא, שהרי בדקוה המים:
Rashi on Sotah 26a:13:1.english: [It is speaking] of one who acts lewdly - After she drank, it was necessary to teach us that she is permitted to her husband, so that you should not say that she is a zonah (a promiscuous woman), since the water tested her.

Rashi on Sotah 26a:13:2.hebrew: מתנוונה - הא ודאי בדקוה המים, וזונה היא, אלא שתלה לה זכות. ואמאי מותרת לבעלה:
Rashi on Sotah 26a:13:2.english: [She] wastes away - Surely the waters tested her and she is a harlot; it is only that [her] merit suspended [the punishment] for her. Why, then, is she permitted to her husband?

Rashi on Sotah 26a:14:1.hebrew: במתנוונה דרך אברים - שאינה מתנוונה במעים ובירכים, אלא ראשה ושאר אבריה כבידים עליה. מהו דתימא, הא לאו זכות תלה לה, דאם כן הוה לה להתנוונה דרך בדיקת המים, אלא באונס זינתה, לפיכך מתנוונה שלא כדרכה, ולכהן מיהא תיתסר:
Rashi on Sotah 26a:14:1.english: Where she wastes away through [her other] limbs - That is, she does not waste away in the intestines and thighs, but rather her head and her other limbs become heavy upon her. [The reason one] might have said [that she is forbidden to her husband]: Surely, [the water] did not [in this case] suspend [the punishment] by merit, for if so, she should have wasted away in the manner of the examination by the water. Rather, she committed adultery under duress; therefore she wastes away in an unusual manner, and she should at least be forbidden to a Kohen.

Rashi on Sotah 26a:15:1.hebrew: מבלעדי אישך - משמע דאישה בר הכי הוא:
Rashi on Sotah 26a:15:1.english: Besides your husband - This implies that her husband is [a man] capable of this.

Rashi on Sotah 26a:15:2.hebrew: קא משמע לן - דלמיקדם שכיבת בעל לבועל הוא דאתא, וסריס בר שכיבה הוא, ואף על גב דלאו בר זריעה הוא. ובסריס חמה קאמר דמותר לקיימה, ולא בסריס אדם שאסור לקיימה משום "לא יבא פצוע דכא" (דברים כג):
Rashi on Sotah 26a:15:2.english: It teaches us - [The verse] comes to [teach that] the husband's intercourse must precede the adulterer's, and a eunuch is capable of intercourse, even though he is not capable of emitting seed. And [the Mishnah] speaks of a eunuch by nature (*saris chamah*), whom it is permitted to keep [as a husband], and not of a eunuch made by man (*saris adam*), whom it is forbidden to keep [as a husband] because of [the verse] "He that is crushed or maimed in his privy parts shall not enter" (Deuteronomy 23).

Rashi on Sotah 26a:1:1.english: Do not drink - For it is written "instead of [her] husband."

Rashi on Sotah 26a:2:1.hebrew: ולא יחזיר עולמית - קנסא קנסוהו רבנן:
Rashi on Sotah 26a:2:1.english: And he may never take her back - The Rabbis penalized him with a fine.

Rashi on Sotah 26a:2:2.hebrew: לכשיגיע זמנו - לאחר כ"ד חדש ללידת הולד:
Rashi on Sotah 26a:2:2.english: When his time arrives - After twenty-four months from the birth of the child.

Rashi on Sotah 26a:3:1.hebrew: והרובא - בחור, כמו ילד (בראשית כא) רביא:
Rashi on Sotah 26a:3:1.english: And the *rova* - A young man, like "a boy" (Genesis 21) [in Aramaic translation: *ravya*]:

Rashi on Sotah 26a:4:1.hebrew: מעוברת עצמו - שהיתה אשתו מעוברת, וקינא לה:
Rashi on Sotah 26a:4:1.english: His own pregnant [wife] - That his wife was pregnant, and he warned her [not to seclude herself with a certain man].

Rashi on Sotah 26a:4:2.english: Or they drink - And we do not say, "Let [the water] not kill the child."

Rashi on Sotah 26a:5:1.hebrew: אשת ממזר לממזר - כלומר, אשה הראויה לממזר, וניסת לממזר, וקינא לה, ונסתרה:
Rashi on Sotah 26a:5:1.english: The wife of a mamzer [who is married] to a mamzer - That is, a woman who is fit [to marry] a mamzer, and she married a mamzer, and he warned her, and she secluded herself [with another man].

Rashi on Sotah 26a:5:2.hebrew: או שותה כו' - ולקמן פריך: פשיטא!
Rashi on Sotah 26a:5:2.english: Or she drinks, etc. - And below [the Gemara] asks: It is obvious!

Rashi on Sotah 26a:6:1.hebrew: אנא דאמרי כי האי תנא - דאית ליה עקרה וזקנה שותות. מדלא נקט אלא איילונית, ונסיב תלמודא מונקתה ונזרעה זרע, ולא משום דאינה ראויה לקיימה, אלמא כרבי אלעזר ס"ל דיכול לישא אחרת ולפרות ולרבות, ואפ"ה איילונית לא:
Rashi on Sotah 26a:6:1.english: I, who say like this Tanna - who holds that a barren woman and an elderly woman drink. [I say this] since [the Mishnah] mentions only an *ayilonit* [and not a barren or elderly woman], and the Talmud takes [the exclusion of an *ayilonit* from the verse] "then she shall be cleared and shall conceive seed" and not because she is unfit to bear children. Evidently, he holds like Rabbi Elazar, that a man may marry another [woman] and be fruitful and multiply, and nevertheless an *ayilonit* does not [drink].

Rashi on Sotah 26a:7:1.hebrew: וזו - כל אשה צנועה עקרה, משום דלא נסתרה הפסידה:
Rashi on Sotah 26a:7:1.english: And this one - Every modest woman would be barren, because by not having been secluded [with another man] she lost out.

Rashi on Sotah 26a:9:1.hebrew: לא ליפוש פסולין - לא נעשה שלום ביניהם. הלואי לא יפרה ולא ירבה, הואיל וכל דורותיו ממזרין:
Rashi on Sotah 26a:9:1.english: Lest we increase the disqualified - We do not make peace between them. Would that he not be fruitful and not multiply, since all his generations are mamzerim.

Tosafot on Sotah 26a:11:1.hebrew: ואמרת ריבויא הוא - תימה, והא אפיקתיה לעיל (סוטה דף כד.) לרבות הארוסה ושומרת יבם לקינוי:
Tosafot on Sotah 26a:11:1.english: "And you shall say – it is an inclusion" - This is astonishing, for didn't we already derive from it above (Sotah 24a) [a teaching] to include a betrothed woman and a woman awaiting levirate marriage in [the law of] warning [by the husband]?

Tosafot on Sotah 26a:12:1.hebrew: וזו הואיל ונתפשה אסורה אימא לא תשתה כלל קמ"ל - תימה לר"י: אמאי לא פריך הכא "ואימא הכי נמי", כדפריך לעיל? ונראה: כל היכא דקרא דמסיק אדעתיה מתוכו למדרש הכי, ומדריש לדרשא אחריתי — לא פריך "ואימא ה"נ", דקמ"ל דכך ניתן למדרש למשה בסיני ולא בע"א; כגון "והיא נתפשה" — לאסור אשת כהן, "מבלעדי אישך" — מי שקדמה שכיבת בעל. אבל לעיל "בני ישראל" משמע בהדיא למעוטי גרים. וכן בפרק שני דיבמות (דף כב.), בגמרא דמי שיש לו אח מ"מ זוקק את אשת אחיו ליבום, דקא פריך: "פשיטא, אחיו הוא! מהו דתימא לילף אחוה אחוה מבני יעקב, קמ"ל" — התם פריך "ואימא הכי נמי", משום דאין גזרה שוה למחצה, וצריך טעמא להוציא מאותה סברא או קרא. וכן לענין ליורשו (שם:) וליטמא לו: "פשיטא, אחיו הוא! סד"א לא יטמא בעל בעמיו — יש בעל שמטמא ויש שאינו מטמא; הא כיצד? מטמא לאשתו כשרה, ואינו מטמא לאשתו פסולה. ה"נ קמ"ל"; ואימא הכי נמי, דהא קרא ממעט פסולין, והאי פסול הוא. וכן בפ"ק דערכין (דף ז.) גבי האשה שיוצאת ליהרג, אין ממתינים לה עד שתלד: "פשיטא, גופה היא! מהו דתימא (כי) 'כאשר ישית עליו בעל האשה' כתיב, והאי ממונא דבעל הוא, קמ"ל" — ואימא ה"נ? דמאי נפקא לן מהתם דממונא דבעל הוא? אבל הכא, כיון דאשמועינן דעיקר קרא לדרשא אחריתי, תו לא סלקי דעתא למעוטי מיניה מידי. וכן פר"י:
Tosafot on Sotah 26a:12:1.english: "And this one — since she was seized, she is forbidden; I might say she should not drink at all; it therefore teaches us" - It is puzzling to Rabbi Yitzchak (the Ri): Why does the Gemara not challenge here, "But say that indeed so [it is]," as it challenged above? And it appears: Wherever the verse, in its own context, is understood to be expounded in this way, and [the Gemara] expounds it for another teaching, it does not challenge, "But say that indeed so [it is]," because [the Gemara] is teaching us that this is how it was given to be expounded to Moses at Sinai, and not otherwise. For example, "and she was seized" — [expounded] to forbid the wife of a priest; "besides your husband" — [expounded as referring to] one whom a husband's intercourse preceded. But above, "the children of Israel" implies explicitly that converts are excluded. And so too in the second chapter of Yevamot (22a), in the Gemara on [the passage] "One who has a brother in any case," [that he obligates his brother's wife to levirate marriage], where it challenges: "It is obvious — he is his brother! What might you have said? Let us derive [by analogy] 'brotherhood, brotherhood' from the sons of Jacob; it therefore teaches us" — there it does challenge, "But say that indeed so [it is]," because there is no half-gezerah shavah, and one needs a reason, from the same logic or a verse, to exclude [him]. And so too regarding inheriting from him (ibid.) and becoming impure for him: "It is obvious — he is his brother! You might have said, 'A husband shall not become impure among his people' — there is a husband who becomes impure and one who does not become impure; how so? He becomes impure for his fit wife, but does not become impure for his unfit wife. This too it teaches us"; and [there it can be asked,] "But say that indeed so [it is]," for the verse excludes the unfit, and this one is unfit. And so too in the first chapter of Arakhin (7a), regarding the woman who is going out to be executed, [where the Mishnah says] they do not wait for her until she gives birth: "It is obvious — she herself [is the one being executed]! What might you have said? (Since) 'as the husband of the woman shall impose upon him' is written, and this [fetus] is the husband's property; it therefore teaches us" — and [there too] one could say, "But say that indeed so [it is]," for what difference does it make to us from there that it is the husband's property? But here, since [the Gemara] has taught us that the main purpose of the verse is for another teaching, it no longer occurs to us to exclude anything from it. And so the Ri explained.

Tosafot on Sotah 26a:15:1.hebrew: אשת סריס - רש"י פי' בסריס חמה, ולא בסריס אדם, שאסור לקיימה. ולא ידעינן מנלן דסריס אדם, כגון ששתה כוס עיקרין, דאסור לקיימה. אי משום האי ברייתא דמייתי בפרק שני דיבמות (דף כ:) ובפרק הערל (שם דף פט:): "פצוע דכא וכרות שפכה, סריס אדם והזקן וכו'" עד "אסור לקיימה" — הא קתני נמי זקן, וכי זקן אסור לקיים? אלא על כרחיך אפצוע דכא וכרות שפכה קאי, כדקתני טעמא משום שנאמר "לא יבא פצוע דכא וכרות שפכה". אבל אסריס דקתני בברייתא, לא ידענא מנליה דקאי נמי עלה:
Tosafot on Sotah 26a:15:1.english: The wife of a eunuch - Rashi explains [this as referring] to a eunuch by nature (saris chamah), and not to a man-made eunuch (saris adam), [for in the latter case] it is forbidden to keep her [as his wife]. But we do not know from where [we derive] that for a man-made eunuch — for example, one who drank a cup of sterilizing roots — it is forbidden to keep her. If it is because of this baraita, which is cited in the second chapter of Yevamot (20b) and in the chapter HaArel (89b): "One whose testicles are crushed, one whose organ is severed, a man-made eunuch, and the old man, etc.," up to "it is forbidden to keep her" — it also says "the old man"; but is it forbidden to keep [a wife of] an old man? Rather, you must say that it refers [only] to one with crushed testicles and one with a severed organ, as [the baraita] states the reason: because it is said, "One whose testicles are crushed or whose organ is severed shall not enter [the congregation of the Lord]" (Deuteronomy 23:2). But as for the "eunuch" mentioned in the baraita, I do not know from where [we know] that it too refers to this.

Tosafot on Sotah 26a:2:1.hebrew: לא ישא אדם מעוברת חבירו - בירושלמי: עליו הכתוב אומר (משלי כ״ג:י׳): "אל תשיג גבול עולם, ובשדה יתומים אל תבא". ומודים חכמים לרבי אלעזר שאם היו לו בנים ואשה [שהיא שותה או לא נוטלת כתובה, היו לו אשה ובנים] ומתו בין קינוי לסתירה — כבר נראית לשתות:
Tosafot on Sotah 26a:2:1.english: A man may not marry another man's pregnant [wife] - In the Yerushalmi: Concerning him, the verse says (Proverbs 23:10): "Do not move back the ancient boundary, and do not enter the fields of orphans." And the Sages agree with Rabbi Elazar that if he had children and a wife [who drinks or does not collect her ketubah; [or: if] he had a wife and children] and they died between the warning and the seclusion, she has already been shown to be fit to drink.

Tosafot on Sotah 26a:3:1.hebrew: [שנשא עקרה וזקינה וכו'] - ותימה: אמאי לא תנא איילונית בהדי עקרה וזקינה:
Tosafot on Sotah 26a:3:1.english: [Who married a barren woman or an old woman, etc.] - And it is astonishing: Why did [the Mishnah] not teach [the case of] an ayilonit (a woman who does not develop female characteristics) together with the barren woman and the old woman?

Tosafot on Sotah 26a:4:1.hebrew: מעוברת עצמו או שותה וכו' - רש"י פי': ולא אמרינן דלא לקטליה לולד. ותימה: אמאי אית לן למקטליה? מה איכפת לן? נמתין עד שתלד! הא תנן בפ"ק דערכין (דף ז.): "האשה היוצאה ליהרג אין ממתינין לה עד שתלד". והתם גזירת הכתוב הוא: "ומתו גם שניהם" — לרבות את הולד. והתם משמע טעמא דרבי קרא; הא לא רבי קרא, לא קטליניה ליה, משום דממונא דבעל הוא, כדכתיב (שמות כ״א:כ״ב): "כאשר ישית עליו בעל האשה". והכא הכי פירושא: מעוברת עצמו, אע"ג דקינא לה כשהיא מעוברת, שותה לאחר שתלד. ולא אמרינן כמו גבי מעוברת חבירו, דאי קינא לה כשהיא מעוברת וילדה ומת הולד או הפילה, אפ"ה אינה שותה, דלאו בת קינוי היתה, דממעט לה בספרי מ"כי תשטה אשתו". וכדאמרינן בירושלמי: לא היו [לו] אשה ובנים וכו', כבר [נראית] שלא לשתות:
Tosafot on Sotah 26a:4:1.english: "[The wife of a man who made her] pregnant himself, or she drinks," etc. - Rashi explains: And we do not say that [we should avoid having her drink so as] not to kill the fetus. And this is astonishing: Why should we have to kill it? What difference does it make to us? Let us wait until she gives birth! Surely we learned in the first chapter of Arakhin (7a): "A woman who is being taken out to be executed — we do not wait for her until she gives birth." But there it is a scriptural decree: "And both of them shall die" — to include the fetus. And there it implies that the reason is that the verse included it; had the verse not included it, we would not kill it, because it is the husband's property, as it is written (Exodus 21:22): "as the husband of the woman shall impose upon him." And here this is the explanation: [In the case of] a woman pregnant by him, even though he warned her while she was pregnant, she drinks after she gives birth. And we do not say, as we do regarding the pregnant wife of another, that if he warned her while she was pregnant and she gave birth and the child died, or she miscarried, even so she does not drink, because she was not subject to warning, since the Sifrei excludes her from "if a man's wife goes astray" (Numbers 5:12). And as we say in the Yerushalmi: If he had no wife and children, etc., it was already [evident] that she should not drink.

Tosafot on Sotah 26a:7:1.hebrew: אמר לו רבי ישמעאל א"כ יסתרו כל עקרות ויפקדו - תימה: ור' ישמעאל לימא ליה לנפשיה: יסתרו כל יולדות בצער וילדו בריוח! וזו הואיל ולא נסתרה הפסידה:
Tosafot on Sotah 26a:7:1.english: Rabbi Yishmael said to him: "If so, all barren women will secrete themselves [with a man] and be remembered [with children]" - This is puzzling: Rabbi Yishmael should have said to himself: [By that logic,] let all women who give birth in pain secrete themselves and give birth with ease! And this woman [i.e., the one who was not secluded], since she did not secrete herself, lost out?
